title: Four in a Row — Minimum Value
source: Reported from the InfyTQ certification coding round (2020) — reconstructed from a GeeksforGeeks 'Infosys Certification Exam Experience | InfyTQ Questions 2020' write-up ('select elements present in four consecutive positions horizontally, vertically or diagonally, return the minimum'). Statement rewritten with precise rules.
statement:
You are given an `R × C` grid of integers.

A value `v` is called a **streak value** if there are **four cells in a straight line, next to each other**, that all contain `v`. "Next to each other in a straight line" means one of the four directions:

- horizontal: `(i, j), (i, j+1), (i, j+2), (i, j+3)`
- vertical: `(i, j), (i+1, j), (i+2, j), (i+3, j)`
- main diagonal: `(i, j), (i+1, j+1), (i+2, j+2), (i+3, j+3)`
- anti-diagonal: `(i, j), (i+1, j-1), (i+2, j-2), (i+3, j-3)`

A longer run (5, 6, … equal cells) also contains four consecutive equal cells, so it counts too.

Print the **minimum** streak value in the grid, or `-1` if the grid has no streak at all.

> Note: a grid may legitimately have `-1` as a streak value; the output is then `-1` as well (it is the true minimum).
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `R` and `C`.
Each of the next `R` lines contains `C` space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Print a single integer — the minimum streak value, or `-1` if none exists.

samples.explanation: `9` fills the main diagonal and `5` fills the anti-diagonal. Both are streak values; the minimum is `5`.
The first row has four `3`s and the last row has five `1`s. The `7`s on the diagonal from `(1,1)` stop after three cells. Minimum streak value is `1`.
No line of four cells fits in a `2 × 3` grid.

hints: For every cell, a streak *starting* there can go in only 4 directions (right, down, down-right, down-left) — checking the other 4 would just find the same streaks again.
For each start cell and direction, verify the 3 following cells are inside the grid and equal to the start value.
Keep a running minimum, and use a sentinel like `None` (not `-1`) for 'nothing found yet' since `-1` can be a real grid value.
editorial:
### Intuition
Every straight run of four equal cells has a unique *first* cell when you scan top-to-bottom, left-to-right, and from that cell the run goes **right**, **down**, **down-right** or **down-left**. So it is enough to try those 4 directions from every cell.

### Approach
For each cell `(i, j)` with value `v` and each direction `(di, dj)` in `{(0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (1,-1)}`:
- check the end cell `(i+3di, j+3dj)` is inside the grid;
- check the 3 next cells equal `v`;
- if so, `best = min(best, v)`.

In Python, fetch the four rows `g[i]..g[i+3]` once per `i` so the inner loop only does list indexing.

### Complexity
`O(4 · R · C)` time, `O(1)` extra space — about 640k checks at the limits.

### Common mistakes
- Forgetting the anti-diagonal (down-left) direction.
- Off-by-one bounds: a run starting at column `j` going right needs `j + 3 < C`; going down-left needs `j ≥ 3`.
- Initialising the answer to `-1` and doing `min(-1, v)` — that breaks for positive values. Track 'found' separately.
